reading.body:
Box has built a portfolio of integrations that let AI agents handle real-world tasks: sending physical mail, managing cloud files, accessing bank data, and exchanging secrets between agents.

These Model Context Protocol tools sit at the boundary between AI systems and the infrastructure they need to operate at scale. An AI agent that can only think cannot process a loan application or onboard an employee. It must read files, verify identity, send documents, and maintain audit trails. Box's integrations bridge this gap by giving agents standardized access to storage, communication channels, and cross-agent coordination. The company's own AI product focuses on enterprise content, but this MCP registry strategy positions it as an operational layer for agentic workflows, where the binding constraint shifts from model capability to the ability to act on real data and systems.

What these integrations do not show is compute or power consumption. They are software abstractions that assume infrastructure exists elsewhere. They do show that AI scaling now depends not only on larger models and more training compute, but on standardized ways for agents to access the human-world interfaces they need to do work. For enterprises, this means the grid constraint on AI is mediated through the systems that connect agents to email, filesystems, banks, and each other.

profile_text.body:
Box is a public company founded in 2005 and headquartered in Redwood City, California. The company describes itself as providing intelligent content management that makes it easy to automate workflows, collaborate internally and externally, and protect sensitive data on one platform. According to its website, Box helps organizations access, share, edit, and co-create content with AI while accelerating productivity, with enterprise-grade security and compliance features to protect sensitive data as teams work together from anywhere.

Box offers Box AI, an enterprise content AI product that provides metadata, governance, compliance, and retention policy capabilities. The company states that Box AI lets users tap into leading AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google for real-time summaries, deep analysis, and smart recommendations. Box also describes its platform as including an intuitive workflow builder for designing and deploying complex processes, AI-driven security with deep learning-based malware detection and automated classification, compliance tools for GDPR, HIPAA, and FINRA requirements, and Box AI Studio for customizing agents to streamline workflows.

As of January 31, 2026, Box reported revenue of $1,177,253,000 according to its 10-K filing. The company trades under the ticker BOX and faces 220 lawsuits in California. Box maintains eight Model Context Protocol servers, providing integrations for email inbox management, object storage, encrypted secret handling, Dropbox file access, MCP routing, cloud storage access, and physical mail capabilities for AI agents.
